seo_title: Party Charcuterie Board Ideas: 18 Boards for Every Occasion
description: 18 party charcuterie board ideas: baby shower, birthday, kids, office party, game day, cocktail and wine parties, grazing tables, cups, jarcuterie, brunch and budget boards, with how much to buy.
answer: Match the board to the party: mild, familiar food with labeled options for showers and office parties, sturdy one-hand bites for game day and cocktails, and several boards or a grazing table for big crowds. Plan about 3 oz each of cheese and meat per guest when the board is the party food, or 2 oz before a meal. Here are 18 ideas.
intro: The party decides the board more than the ingredients do. A baby shower needs pregnancy-safe options, the office party needs labels, game day needs food that survives being eaten with one hand while watching the TV, and 50 people need more than one board.
The ideas below are grouped by kind of party. Each links to a full guide or board page with what to buy and how to set it up.

sections.heading: How to choose the right party board

items.text: two or three boards, or one board plus cups or skewers.
stations or a [grazing table](/blog/grazing-table/), so people aren't all crowded around one spot.
familiar food, and label anything with nuts, gluten or pork. The [Diet Checker](/dietary/) helps.

sections.heading: How much to buy for a party
paras: When the board is the party food, plan about 3 oz of cheese and 3 oz of meat per guest, plus 10–12 crackers. Before a meal, 2 oz of each and 6–8 crackers is enough. From 20 guests, add about 10%.
For exact totals for your guest count, use the [Party Planner](/party-planner/), or see [how much charcuterie per person](/blog/how-much-charcuterie-per-person/).

sections.heading: Keeping a board fresh through a long party
paras: Don't put everything out at once. Set out about half, keep the rest covered in the fridge and refill after an hour or two. Cheese, meat and dips shouldn't sit out for more than 2 hours.
Add crackers and anything sliced, like apples and pears, last so they stay crisp and don't brown.

items.lead: One huge board for a big crowd.
items.text: Everyone crowds one corner. Split the food into stations.
Label the board, and keep a vegetarian or nut-free section.
At parties, the familiar things go first. Spend on one special cheese and keep the rest crowd-pleasers.
Crackers and bread run out before the cheese does. Buy more than you think.

faq.q: How much charcuterie do I need for a party?
faq.a: About 3 oz each of cheese and meat per guest when the board is the main party food, or 2 oz each before a meal. For 20 guests as party food, that's about 4 lb of cheese and 4 lb of meat, including 10% extra for a crowd.

faq.q: How many charcuterie boards do I need for 50 people?
faq.a: Plan on stations rather than one board: three or four boards around the room, or a grazing table built in sections.

faq.q: What's the best charcuterie board for a baby shower?
faq.a: One with mild, pasteurized cheeses and fruit for everyone, plus a labeled pregnancy-safe section with no cold cured meat. See the [pregnancy-safe board guide](/blog/pregnancy-safe-charcuterie-board/).

faq.q: How far ahead can I make a party charcuterie board?
faq.a: Slice cheese and fold meat the day before and keep them covered in the fridge. Assemble the board within an hour of the party and add crackers last.

faq.q: What's a good charcuterie idea for an office party?
faq.a: Familiar cheeses and meats, fruit, crackers and pretzels, with labels for anything with nuts, gluten or pork. Cups or skewers work well when people are standing.

faq.q: What's the difference between a grazing table and a charcuterie board?
faq.a: A grazing table covers a whole table and feeds 20 to 100+ people, built in sections. A charcuterie board is one board. See [grazing board vs charcuterie board](/blog/grazing-board-vs-charcuterie-board/).
